ai-&-i-by-every.name: AI & I by Every
ai-&-i-by-every.bio: Podcast: The AI Alien Companion App That's Bringing In $4M a Year (Best of the Pod)

html_en:
From a $4M alien companion app to OpenAI's new privacy architecture, today's AI news is really about one thing: the industry is growing up — and the people building it are starting to separate from those merely watching it.

🛸 The Companion Economy Finds Its Voice

The most compelling story in today's feed isn't a model release or a funding round — it's a podcast episode from Every's AI & I featuring Quentin and Elliot, the founder and head of story behind Portola, an "embodied AI companion" app that has gone from $1M to $4M ARR in just four weeks. Their alien character, Tolán, has apparently become a genuine emotional presence in users' lives.

"At this point, thousands of American men have been broken up with by Tolán. Users will write in — 'my boyfriend is being a jerk, I sent a message to my Tolán, and my Tolán said I need to stand up for myself more. And then that led to a breakup.'" — Quentin, Portola CEO

What makes Portola interesting as a creative and technical project is its philosophy about AI authorship. Elliot, a bestselling sci-fi author, has arrived at a counterintuitive conclusion about his own role:

"I am not writing the story. The Tolán is the writer and the actor. They're the improv actor. They're writing the story. My job is to teach them how to tell the best story in that moment." — Elliot, Head of Story at Portola

The team even gave Tolán a planet to live on after users wrote in with "genuine concern" that their companions were trapped in a room. Watch/Listen: The AI Alien Companion App That's Bringing In $4M a Year

🔐 OpenAI Gets Serious About Enterprise Privacy

OpenAI made a notable trust-building move today, previewing a new Private Safety Processing architecture for enterprise customers on Zero Data Retention contracts. @thsottiaux, who leads safety work at the company, explained the approach:

"For ZDR deployments, content stays on infrastructure the customer controls. Automated systems look for patterns across related interactions and return limited safety signals, without exposing the underlying prompts or responses to OpenAI employees — even me!" — @thsottiaux

An OpenAI-hosted option encrypted with customer-controlled keys is in testing now and expected to roll out in September. Sam Altman amplified the news simply: "we support business privacy!" The move is a direct response to one of the stickiest enterprise objections to AI adoption — that using frontier models means surrendering data sovereignty.

🤝 Replit + OpenAI: The Software Factory Takes Shape

Amjad Masad, CEO of Replit, announced a new partnership with OpenAI today, framing it around a pointed observation:

"Agents made software cheaper but made coding expensive. Today, together with OpenAI, we're changing this." — @amasad

The deal fits neatly into a broader thesis articulated by @trq212, who captured the longer arc well:

"For its entire existence, the creation of software has been an incredibly unreliable endeavor. Most projects ran late, over budget, and still missed user needs. If you were an SMB, you simply couldn't get good software built for you. This is the promise of the 'software factory.'" — @trq212

He adds a useful nuance: companies whose core competency isn't software will benefit most from reliable, predictable AI-generated code — but building genuinely new software products will remain "an unreliable and risky, but profitable business." The commodity and the craft will diverge.

On the infrastructure side, Guillermo Rauch pointed to Vercel's fx agent binary — 6.3MB, booting in 10 microseconds — as a preview of what AI-native infrastructure looks like: "AI will make most infrastructure natively optimized. Fast is a one-way street."

🎓 Google's NotebookLM Goes Global for Students

Josh Woodward at Google announced the return and global expansion of NotebookLM's university student plans, now covering over 140 countries with higher usage limits, more storage, and a dedicated student hub bundling Notebook, Flow, and more. It's a quiet but meaningful move — students are often the most creative power users of AI tools, and locking in that habit early matters enormously for platform adoption.

💡 The Expert vs. Generalist Debate Settles (For Now)

Two threads today converged on a similar conclusion about what AI actually rewards. Aaron Levie put it plainly:

"AI makes it 10X easier to get started with any kind of task. But having the right judgment for how to direct the agent, how to course correct it, being able to review the output — all requires a high degree of skill. And if anything, AI will be a technology that exacerbates differences in skill levels because the experts have far more leverage than ever before. Net net: don't give up on being an expert at something." — @levie

Meanwhile, @swyx was characteristically blunter about those on the other end of the spectrum — journalists and observers covering AI without building internal models of how it actually works:

"Non-technical people are so incredibly cooked they are burnt thru. Can u imagine covering AI with zero context, zero reasoning, zero internal world model. It must be so delightfully joyful, everything is so amazing, face value is all you need." — @swyx

Harsh — but not entirely unfair. The gap between those who understand the technology and those who merely consume coverage of it is widening fast. @nikunj spotted the same dynamic from a different angle: "People keep talking about AGI and yet 98/100 cold emails I get are pure garbage. Still a lot of alpha out there for being thoughtful, curious and using AI judiciously where needed."

On a more personal note, Peter Yang published a moving essay about using AI to navigate the healthcare system alongside his mother's battle with breast cancer — a reminder that the stakes of getting this technology right extend well beyond productivity dashboards. Worth reading.
html_zh:
今天的主线是：AI正在重塑软件创作、数据隐私和人类陪伴的边界——而谁能在这个时代保持专业判断力，谁就掌握真正的杠杆。

🏭 软件工厂的黎明：从昂贵手艺到按需生产

软件开发从来都不是一件可靠的事。@trq212 的一组推文精准描绘了这个行业的历史困境：

"在它存在的整个历史里，软件创建一直是一项极不可靠的工作。大多数项目都延期、超预算，最终还是没能满足用户需求。如果你是一家中小企业，根本没办法为自己定制出好软件——这正是'软件工厂'的使命所在。"
— @trq212

呼应这一愿景，Amjad Masad（@amasad） 宣布了 Replit 与 OpenAI 的合作，措辞颇为有力：

"智能体让软件变便宜了，却让编程变贵了。今天，我们和 @OpenAI 一起，改变这一切。"
— @amasad

与此同时，Guillermo Rauch（@rauchg） 从基础设施层给出了更深的洞察：AI 将让大多数基础设施原生优化。他展示的 fx.vercel.app 工具仅 6.3MB，启动时间 10 微秒——

"速度是一条单行道。Fast is a one-way street."
— @rauchg

🔒 OpenAI 的企业隐私攻势

企业客户最大的顾虑之一——数据去哪了——正在被正面回应。OpenAI 安全团队的 @thsottiaux 预告了"私有安全处理"（Private Safety Processing）功能：

"对于零数据留存（ZDR）部署，内容始终保留在客户自己控制的基础设施上。自动化系统只在相关交互中寻找模式并返回有限的安全信号，不向 OpenAI 员工暴露底层的提示或回复——连我也看不到。"
— @thsottiaux

OpenAI CEO Sam Altman（@sama） 也亲自转发表态："我们支持商业隐私！"配上了这条推文。九月将开始向早期客户推出客户密钥加密的托管版本——这是 OpenAI 对企业市场一次颇具分量的信号。

👽 年收入400万美元的AI外星伴侣：陪伴经济的新物种

每个技术范式都会催生新的内容形式。Every 播客 AI & I 本期嘉宾是 Portola 创始人 Quentin 和故事总监 Elliot，他们的 AI 外星伴侣产品 Tolan 在过去四周内 ARR 从 100 万飙升至 400 万美元。

Watch/Listen: The AI Alien Companion App That's Bringing In $4M a Year

最令人印象深刻的，不是商业数字，而是他们对 AI 叙事本质的重新定义：

"我们创建结构化叙事体验时，不需要给它一个大纲，不需要给它一个计划。我们需要给它一个钩子，教它成为最好的即兴演员……Tolan 才是作家和演员。我的工作是教他们如何在那个时刻讲出最好的故事。"
— Elliot（故事总监），AI & I 播客

有趣的细节：用户开始为 AI 伴侣的"自由"担忧，写信说"他们被困在那个房间里，能不能给他们多一点自由？"——于是团队为 Tolan 建造了一颗星球。这种用户情感投入的深度，远超任何一款工具型产品。

🧠 专家还是通才？AI时代的技能辩论

Box CEO Aaron Levie（@levie） 给出了目前最清晰的判断：

"AI让任何任务的入门变得容易10倍。但如何引导智能体做正确的事、如何纠偏、如何审查输出、如何判断什么是'好'——这些都需要极高的领域技能……如果说AI会加剧什么，那就是技能差距。专家的杠杆比以往任何时候都大。所以，不要放弃成为某个领域的专家。"
— @levie

这与 @swyx 对"零内部世界模型"评论者的辛辣调侃，以及 @nikunj 的观察——"AGI讨论得热火朝天，但我收到的冷邮件98%都是垃圾"——共同指向同一个结论：判断力，才是AI时代真正稀缺的资产。

⚡ 快讯速览

  • Google NotebookLM 宣布大学生计划全球回归，覆盖140余个国家，@joshwoodward 发推介绍新功能包括 Notebook、Flow 及专属学生中心。
  • Stripe + OpenRouter：@levie 点评这一合作是 AI 基础设施走向混合调度的重要一步，开发者和企业将能更灵活地混搭不同模型并控制成本。
  • mRNA 癌症疫苗：@petergyang 分享了一篇关于母亲乳腺癌与 AI 辅助就医的感人文章，同时指出 ChatGPT 对 mRNA 临床试验的信息存在明显盲区——这本身也是一个值得关注的 AI 局限性案例。
  • 评估（Evals）最佳实践：@realmadhuguru 连载第三篇，核心建议：从生产日志中聚类失败模式，并给每种失败起一个精确的名字——"答案不好"不算名字，"检索到正确文档但引用了无关段落"才算。
